title: MV/MZ One-Click Import/Export Multi-Language Text Tool

posts.author: CHIMAKI
posts.body:
I am developing a tool for quickly
exporting and importing text
, which will help more games support
multi-language localization
(or
multiple languages
).
Many developers choose to publish their games on Steam. However, Steam is an international platform, and only having your native language as the game's text can lead to
losing many opportunities for exposure
.
Although there are existing localization tools on the market, such as
DKTools' Localization Tool
, and I have even written my own plugin to support localized text, the multi-language plugin I wrote primarily requires the following steps, which align with my own game development habits:
Plan the text
on Excel first.
Write special syntax
into RPG Maker.
Translate the multi-language text
on Excel.
Implement it into the game
to support multiple languages.
However, I know that the workflow for most developers I know, especially regarding text, is almost always this:
They
write their native language directly into RPG Maker
.
They
complete the game development
.
They then
decide they want to create a multi-language version
.
They
duplicate the project
and create separate versions for different languages. (I strongly discourage this approach because you will inevitably need to fix bugs after release. This method forces you to maintain far too many versions simultaneously, which will certainly lead to burnout.)
Returning to the main point, for developers using the second development model (writing text directly), I usually recommend using the DKTools localization utility. It's fast and convenient. So, why am I creating this new tool?
It is mainly designed to
suit my own development habits
and to be used by developers familiar with my multi-language plugin. Its features are as follows:
Features
​
One-click export
of all text to CSV.
One-click import
of all text as multi-language codes.
In-game language switching
is supported directly.
After inserting the multi-language code (\T[xxx]),
your native language text will automatically be added as a comment
(or
note
).
Here is a quick demonstration of me using this tool. Everything is ready in about 2 minutes.[Video/Image demonstrating the tool]
The
Normal Usage Flow
is roughly as follows:
Game is
completed
.
Export
the multi-language CSV.
CSV is sent to
professional translators
for translation.
Import
the multi-language CSV.
＃My native language is not English, so the article contains a lot of machine translation.
